item.title: CVE-2026-121744 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.0: 7.8
item.description:
Thursday 12 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.0: 7.8 | Ashlar-Vellum Cobalt XE File Parsing Stack-based Buffer Overflow Remote Code Execution Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code on affected installations of Ashlar-Vellum Cobalt. User interaction is required to exploit this vulnerability in that the target must visit a malicious page or open a malicious file.
The specific flaw exists within the parsing of XE files. The issue results from the lack of proper validation of the length of user-supplied data prior to copying it to a stack-based buffer. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to execute code in the context of the current process. Was ZDI-CAN-28172.

item.title: CVE-2026-126795 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 5.5
item.description: Thursday 12 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 5.5 | A vulnerability was determined in ToolJet up to 3.20.256-lts/3.21.93-beta. The impacted element is the function activateUserWithPassword of the file server/src/modules/onboarding/util.service.ts of the component Onboarding Signup Endpoint. Executing a manipulation of the argument email can lead to missing authentication. It is possible to launch the attack remotely. The exploit has been publicly disclosed and may be utilized. Upgrading to version 3.21.94-beta is sufficient to resolve this issue. This patch is called af8f17a745621ae418f1743440f63d315e8b8643. The affected component should be upgraded. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure.

item.title: CVE-2026-126957 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 6.9
item.description: Thursday 12 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 6.9 | An integer underflow in Zephyr's IPv4 option handling allows a remote, unauthenticated attacker to read stack memory. When replying to an ICMP Echo Request that carries an IPv4 Record Route or Timestamp option, icmpv4_update_record_route() and icmpv4_update_time_stamp() in subsys/net/ip/icmpv4.c compute the length of the already recorded data as ptr - ptr_offset in uint8_t arithmetic. The attacker-controlled Pointer field is checked against the option length but not against the RFC 791 minimum (4 for Record Route, 5 for Timestamp), so a smaller value wraps the length to up to 252 bytes. net_pkt_write() then reads past the 40-byte opt_data stack buffer and up to 213 bytes of stack memory, which can include stack and heap pointers, are returned in the ICMP Echo Reply. A single packet triggers the leak and the device does not crash, so it can be repeated. Devices built with CONFIG_NET_IPV4_HDR_OPTIONS, which CONFIG_NET_IPV4_IGMP selects, are affected.

item.title: CVE-2026-13269 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.0: 7.5

This vulnerability allows remote attackers to create a denial-of-service condition on affected installations of Quest NetVault Backup. Authentication is not required to exploit this vulnerability.
The specific flaw exists within the StnzCreateKey function. The issue results from the lack of proper validation of user-supplied data, which can result in a numeric truncation error before allocating a buffer. item.title: CVE-2026-111433 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 8.6
item.description:
Thursday 12 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 8.6 | UNIX symbolic link (symlink) following vulnerability in openEuler iSulad on Linux.
This vulnerability is associated with program file src/daemon/modules/spec/specs_mount.c.
This issue affects iSulad: through 2.1.6.
If an attacker can get the victim or the platform to run their crafted malicious image, they can cause the iSulad daemon to copy sensitive host directories into an anonymous volume when creating a container, which the container can then read.

item.title: CVE-2026-111434 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 5.6
item.description:
Thursday 12 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 5.6 | Use of Externally-Controlled format string vulnerability in openEuler iSulad on Linux.
This vulnerability is associated with program file src/daemon/modules/image/oci/oci_load.c.
This issue affects iSulad: through 2.1.6.
When the iSulad daemon performs container lifecycle operations (such as create, start, exec, stop, etc.) through the isula runtime (shim), the daemon reads the stderr output of the shim process via a pipe for error information display. If the buffer contains format specifiers such as %s, %x, or %n, it may trigger a format string vulnerability, potentially leading to information leakage, denial of service, or the risk of arbitrary writes.

item.title: CVE-2026-111435 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 7.4
item.description:
Thursday 12 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 7.4 | Relative path traversal vulnerability in openEuler iSulad on Linux.
This vulnerability is associated with program file src/daemon/modules/image/oci/oci_load.c.
This issue affects iSulad: through 2.1.6.
In oci_load.c, oci_load_process_manifest() does not sanitize the Config path of manifest.json. A malicious tar package can enable the isulad with the root permission to read any file on the host.

item.title: CVE-2026-111436 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 4.4
item.description:
Thursday 12 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 4.4 | Missing release of memory after effective lifetime vulnerability in openEuler iSulad on Linux.
This vulnerability is associated with program file src/daemon/modules/spec/specs_mount.c.
This issue affects iSulad: through 2.1.6.
The memory leak vulnerability causes the iSulad daemon to be triggered frequently, exhausting the host machine's memory and ultimately leading to an OOM crash of the daemon, resulting in a denial of service (DoS).
